newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian anti-Miss World protester dies in flames.
newsitem.headline: Indian anti-Miss World protester dies in flames.

text.p: A 24-year-old man died on Thursday after setting himself ablaze in a human-torch protest against India staging the Miss World beauty pageant, witnesses said.
Suresh Kumar, an unemployed tailor, shouted anti-pageant slogans as he set fire to himself in front of hundreds of people in the heart of the southern city of Madurai, they said.
He doused himself in chemicals and was engulfed by flames in seconds before anyone could stop him, according to local reporters.
Kumar, a member of the extremist Marxist-led Democratic Youth Federation of India, died in hospital with 90 percent burns.
Police went on alert to prevent any disorderly reaction in Bangalore, the southern Indian city which hosts this year's Miss World, some 432 km (270 miles) north of Madurai.
"We are on guard. It may have repercussions here," G.K.Bekal, deputy commissioner of police, in charge of security for the show, told Reuters.
Police were deployed in strength around various venues where the contestants are appearing in the run up to the finale on November 23.
The 89 beauties were attending a charity ball in the city on Thursday night, following an appearance at a children's gala earlier in the day.
The pageant has attracted protests ever since Indian film superstar Amitabh Bachchan announced it would be held in India for the first time in the show's 45-year history.
"The incident is regrettable. Our sympathies go out to the family of the deceased," said a spokesman for Amitabh Bachchan Corporation Ltd., the contest's organisers.
He believed, however, the incident would not affect the schedule of the Miss World pageant.
Around 12,000 policemen will safeguard the event, which drew an estimated two billion television viewers last year.
More than 20 organisations have come out against the event, opposing it on grounds ranging from protests against the commercialisation of women to the so-called contamination of Indian culture.
A women's organisation, the Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women), has already threatened its members will commit suicide by self-immolation in protest against the show.
"We will sneak into the stadium and burn ourselves. We have already bought tickets," K.N. Shashikala, of the Mahila Jagran Samiti, told Reuters last week.
A petition by the Mahila Jagran Samiti to ban the show will be heard in court on Friday.
And local members of parliament for the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have said they will lay siege to Chinnaswamy cricket stadium where the crowning ceremony will take place.
The militant Farmers' Association has also threatened to torch the stadium.
The furore had already forced the Miss World organisers to hold the swimsuit parade outside India earlier this month, in the Seychelles Islands in the Indian Ocean.
The contestants arrived in Bangalore in the early hours of Tuesday morning, amid a massive security operation.

Bangalore police have detained 40 people as a preventive measure against potential trouble, and have issued orders that rallies or demonstrations of more than 10 people will be unlawful until the Miss World show has quit the city.
